source_text: οἰκουμένη. Βαροὺχ ἀποκλαιόμενος τὸν λαὸν ὄντα ἐν γῇ Χαλδαίων τῶν πνεῦμα ἅγιον μὴ ἐχόντων βοᾷ. «τί σοί ἐστιν, Ἰσραήλ, ὅτι ἐν γῇ τῶν ἐχθρῶν εἶ;: ἐπαλαιώθης ἐν γῇ ἀλλοτρίᾳ, συνεμιάνθης τοῖς νεκροῖς, προσελογίσθης μετὰ τῶν εἰς Ἅιδου. ἐγκατέλιπες πηγὴν τῆς σοφίας· τῇ ὁδῷ τοῦ θεοῦ εἰ ἐπορεύθης, κατῴκεις ἂν ἐν εἰρήνῃ τὸν αἰῶνα χρόνον·» «πηγὴν» τὸν θεόν, «σοφίαν» τὸ ἅγιον πνεῦμα λέγων. Ἰωάννης ἀπὸ τοῦ υἱοῦ πρὸς τὴν Σαμαρίτιδα. «εἰ ᾔδεις τὴν δωρεὰν τοῦ θεοῦ, καὶ τίς ἐστιν ὁ λέγων σοι· δός μοι πιεῖν, σὺ ἂν ᾔτησας αὐτόν, καὶ ἔδωκεν ἄν σοι ὕδωρ ζῶν·» τῆς κολυμβήθρας τοῦ ἁγίου πνεύματος τὰ ἀθάνατα νάματα λέγων. ὅτι γὰρ πάντα ταῦτα περὶ τοῦ πνεύματος τοῦ θεοῦ εἴρηται, ὃ μνημονευθεὶς εὐαγγελιστὴς ἡρμήνευσεν ἐπὶ λέξεως· τοῦ γὰρ σωτῆρος εἰπόντος· «εἴ τις διψᾷ, ἐρχέσθω πρὸς μὲ καὶ πινέτω. ὁ πιστεύων εἰς ἐμὲ καθὼς εἶπεν ἡ γραφή, ποταμοὶ ἐκ τῆς κοιλίας αὐτοῦ ῥεύσουσιν ὕδατος ζῶντος,» εὐθὺς ἐπήγαγεν· «τοῦτο δὲ εἶπεν περὶ τοῦ πνεύματος, οὗ ἔμελλον λαμβάνειν οἱ πιστεύσαντες εἰς αὐτόν.» 6.23ν ὅτι τῷ ἁγίῳ πνεύματι ἐχρίσθη ὁ σωτήρ· οὐκ ἂν δὲ εἰ κτίσμα ἦν, τῷ ἰδίῳ ἐχρίσατο ποιήματι ὁ ἄκτιστος; καὶ ὅτι καὶ ἡμεῖς χρῖσμα ἔχομεν αὐτοῦ. ἡ κτίσις ἐλαίῳ κτιστῷ ἁγιαζομένῳ βαπτίσματι χρίεται. ὁ σωτήρ, ὡς θεὸς, τῷ συνακτίστῳ αὐτοῦ ἐχρίσατο παναγίῳ πνεύματι παρὰ τοὺς μετόχους ἡμᾶς. εἰ γὰρ κτίσμα ἦν, οὐκ ἂν τῷ ἰδίῳ ἐχρίσατο ποιήματι ὁ ἄκτιστος; μάρτυρες δὲ οἱ ὑπογεγραμμένοι· Ἠσαῖας ἀπὸ τοῦ σωτῆρος λέγων· «πνεῦμα κυρίου 67 ἐπ' ἐμέ, οὗ εἵνεκεν ἔχρισέ με·» ∆αυὶδ δέ· «διὰ τοῦτο ἔχρισέν σε ὁ θεός, ὁ θεός σου ἔλαιον ἀγαλλιάσεως παρὰ τοὺς μετόχους σου.» διὰ τοῦτο ποῖον; ἐπειδὴ θεὸς ἀχειροποίητος ὢν ὑπὸ θεοῦ ἀκτίστου ἀνάρχου ἐχρίσθη. εἶπεν δὲ τὸ «ὁ θεός σου» διὰ τὴν ἐκ παρθένου γέννησιν αὐτοῦ. Πέτρος ἐν ταῖς πράξεσιν· «ὑμεῖς ἐπίστασθε τὸ γενόμενον ῥῆμα καθ' ὅλης τῆς Ἰουδαίας καὶ Σαμαρείας, ἀρξάμενον ἀπὸ τῆς Γαλιλαίας μετὰ τὸ βάπτισμα, ὃ ἐκή ρυξεν Ἰωάννης· Ἰησοῦν τὸν ἀπὸ Ναζαρέθ, ὡς ἔχρισεν αὐτὸν ὁ θεὸς πνεύματι ἁγίῳ καὶ δυνάμει·» αἱ Πράξεις· «συνήχθησαν ἐπ' ἀληθείας ἐν τῇ πόλει ταύτῃ, ἐπὶ τὸν ἅγιον παῖδα σου Ἰησοῦν, ὃν ἔχρισας.» καὶ τὰ Ἄισματα δὲ περὶ τούτου ὑφηγεῖται οὑτωσί· «μύρον ἐκκενωθὲν ὄνομά σοι· διὰ τοῦτο νεάνιδες ἠγάπησάν σε.» «μύρου» ὄνομα εἶναι τῷ Χριστῷ λέγει τὸ τοῦ παρακλήτου· ἐπειδὴ ἄμφω αἱ ὑποστάσεις τοῦ τε ὀνόματος κοινωνοῦσιν καὶ ἐν ἑαυταῖς τὴν τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ πατρὸς εὐωδιάζουσιν φύσιν. «νεανίδας» δὲ τὰς ἐκκλησίας λέγει, ἐν αἷς δοξάζεται, περὶ ὧν καὶ ∆αυὶδ ἐν ξζʹ εἶπεν ψαλμῷ· «προέφθασαν ἄρχοντες, ἐχόμενοι ψαλλόντων, ἐν μέσῳ νεανίδων τυμπα νιστριῶν·» οὕτω φράσας διὰ τὸ ἐκβόητον τῆς πίστεως καὶ διὰ τὸ ἠχεῖν αὐτὰς εἰς πᾶσαν τὴν γῆν τοῖς ἀναγνώσμασιν καὶ ταῖς ψαλμῳδίαις. πρὸς ἑκάστην δὲ αὐτῶν ἐν τοῖς Ἄισμασι καὶ αὐτὸς ὁ ὡραῖος τῷ κάλλει νυμφίος σωφρόνως προσλαλεῖ· «ἰδοὺ εἶ καλὴ ἡ πλησίον μου, ἰδοὺ εἶ καλή.» καὶ πάλιν ἐπιθαλάμιον ὥσπερ ᾄδει· «δεῦρο ἀπὸ λιβάνου, νύμφη· δεῦρο ἀπὸ λιβάνου· ἐλεύσῃ καὶ διελεύσῃ ἀπὸ ἀρχῆς πίστεως.» ὅτι δὲ καὶ ἡμεῖς χρῖσμα δεχόμεθα ἐν τῷ ἀνακαινισμῷ, Ἰωάννης γράφει ἐν τῇ πρώτῃ ἐπιστολῇ· «καὶ ὑμεῖς χρῖσμα ἔχετε ἀπὸ τοῦ ἁγίου καὶ οἴδατε πάντα.» ὥσπερ, φησίν, ἐν τῇ οἰκονομίᾳ ὁ σωτήρ, καὶ «ὑμεῖς χρῖσμα ἔχετε ἀπὸ τοῦ ἁγίου» πνεύματος. καὶ τοῦτο δὲ τὸ σωτήριον δῶρον κοινῇ ὑπὸ τῆς μακαρίας τριάδος ἡμῖν παρεσχῆσθαι, διδάσκουσιν οὕτως· Ἠσαῖας· «καὶ ποιήσει κύριος Σαβαὼθ πᾶσιν τοῖς ἔθνεσιν ἐπὶ τὸ ὄρος τοῦτο, πίονται οἶνον, χρίσονται μύρον ἐν τῷ ὄρει τούτῳ. παράδος ταῦτα πάν τα τοῖς ἔθνεσιν.» «ὄρος» γὰρ τὴν ἐκκλησίαν τοῦ θεοῦ διὰ τὸ ὑψηλὸν τῆς πίστεως, «οἶνον» τὸ δεσποτικὸν σωτήριον αἷμα, «μύρον», ὃ ἁγιασθέντες ἀλειφόμεθα ὑπὸ τοῦ ἱερέως προανεφώνησεν. Ἰωάννης ἐν τῇ αὐτῇ πρώτῃ ἐπιστολῇ περὶ τοῦ Χριστοῦ· «καὶ ὑμεῖς τὸ χρῖσμα, ὃ ἐλάβετε ἀπ' αὐτοῦ, μένει ἐν ὑμῖν· καὶ οὐ χρείαν ἔχετε, ἵνα τις διδάσκῃ ὑμᾶς, ἀλλ' ὡς τὸ αὐτοῦ χρῖσμα διδάσκει ὑμᾶς περὶ πάντων,» Παῦλος δὲ ἐν τῇ δευτέρᾳ πρὸς Κορινθίους· «ὁ δὲ βεβαιῶν ἡμᾶς σὺν ὑμῖν εἰς Χριστόν, καὶ χρίσας ἡμᾶς θεός, καὶ σφραγισάμενος ἡμᾶς, καὶ δοὺς τὸν ἀρραβῶνα τοῦ πνεύματος ἐν ταῖς καρδίαις ἡμῶν.» 7.ν Περὶ τῶν θεϊκῶν ἐνεργειῶν καὶ παροχῶν τοῦ ἁγίου πνεύματος Ἄγαν τοίνυν φιλοτίμως τὴν θεῖαν καὶ ἀκροτάτην τοῦ ἁγίου πνεύματος φύσιν τὴν οὖσαν ὑπὲρ ζωὴν καὶ ὑπὲρ νοῦν· τὰ λόγια ἐπιδείξαντα ἐφάμιλλον αὐτῆς καὶ τὴν
pass_a_gloss: [Continuing from the previous section: ... what each city is for men, this for the Almighty is the] inhabited world. Baruch, lamenting the people being in the land of the Chaldeans, who do not have Holy Spirit, cries: 'what is it to you, Israel, that you are in the land of the enemies? You grew old in a foreign land, you were defiled together with the dead, you were reckoned with those into Hades. You abandoned the fountain of wisdom; if you had walked in the way of God, you would be dwelling in peace for the age of time,' saying 'fountain' for God, 'wisdom' for the Holy Spirit. John from the Son to the Samaritan woman: 'if you knew the gift of God, and who it is who says to you: give me to drink, you would have asked him, and he would have given you living water,' saying [this of] the immortal streams of the font of the Holy Spirit. For that all these things are said about the Spirit of God, the evangelist who has been mentioned interpreted expressly; for when the Saviour had said: 'if anyone thirsts, let him come to me and drink. The one believing in me, as the Scripture said, rivers of living water will flow from his belly,' at once he added: 'and this he said about the Spirit, which those who believed in him were going to receive.' 6.23ν [Chapter title:] That the Saviour was anointed with the Holy Spirit; and if it were a creature, would not the uncreated have been anointed with his own thing made? And that we too have his anointing. The creation is anointed with created oil being sanctified in baptism. The Saviour, as God, was anointed with his co-uncreated all-holy Spirit beyond us the partakers. For if it were a creature, would not the uncreated have been anointed with his own thing made? And witnesses are those written below: Isaiah saying from the Saviour: 'Spirit of the Lord [page number 67, debris] upon me, on account of which he anointed me'; and David: 'on account of this God, your God, anointed you with oil of gladness beyond your partakers.' On account of this what? Since, being God not made by hand, he was anointed by God uncreated, beginningless. And he said the 'your God' because of his birth from a virgin. Peter in the Acts: 'you know the word that came to be throughout all Judea and Samaria, having begun from Galilee after the baptism which John preached [the word split across a line]: Jesus the one from Nazareth, how God anointed him with Holy Spirit and power'; the Acts: 'they were gathered in truth in this city against your holy servant Jesus, whom you anointed.' And the Songs too guide about this thus: 'your name is ointment emptied out; for this reason maidens loved you.' It says that the name of 'ointment' belongs to Christ, that of the Paraclete; since both the hypostases share in the name and in themselves give off as fragrance the nature of God and Father. And 'maidens' it says are the churches, in which he is glorified, about which David also spoke in the 67th psalm (LXX; English 68): 'rulers went ahead, holding close to those singing psalms, in the midst of maidens playing timbrels [the word split across a line],' having phrased it thus because of the loudly proclaimed renown of the faith and because of their sounding into all the earth with the readings and the psalmodies. And to each of them in the Songs the bridegroom himself, fair in beauty, speaks chastely: 'behold you are fair, my near one, behold you are fair.' And again he sings as it were a wedding song: 'come here from Lebanon, bride; come here from Lebanon; you will come and pass through from the beginning of faith.' And that we too receive anointing in the renewal, John writes in the first letter: 'and you have anointing from the Holy One and you know all things.' As, he says, in the dispensation the Saviour, also 'you have anointing from the Holy' Spirit. And that this saving gift too has been furnished to us in common by the blessed Trinity, they teach thus: Isaiah: 'and the Lord Sabaoth will make for all the nations upon this mountain, they will drink wine, they will be anointed with ointment on this mountain. Hand over all these things to the nations [the word split across a line].' For 'mountain' the Church of God because of the height of the faith, 'wine' the Lord's saving blood, 'ointment', with which, having been sanctified, we are anointed by the priest, he proclaimed beforehand. John in the same first letter about Christ: 'and you, the anointing which you received from him remains in you; and you do not have need that anyone teach you, but as his anointing teaches you about all things'; and Paul in the second to Corinthians: 'and the one confirming us with you into Christ, and having anointed us, God, and having sealed us, and having given the pledge of the Spirit in our hearts.' 7.ν [Chapter title:] On the divine activities and provisions of the Holy Spirit. Very generously then, the divine and highest nature of the Holy Spirit, the one being above life and above mind, the oracles having shown, as a match for it also the [continues in the next unit] ...
pass_b_english: Baruch, weeping over the people who were in the land of the Chaldeans, who did not have the Holy Spirit, cries out: “What is it with you, Israel, that you are in the land of your enemies? You have grown old in a foreign land, you have been defiled with the dead, you have been counted with those in Hades. You have forsaken the fountain of wisdom. If you had walked in the way of God, you would have dwelt in peace for ever” (Baruch 3:10-13). By “fountain” he means God, and by “wisdom” the Holy Spirit.

John, giving the Son’s words to the Samaritan woman: “If you knew the gift of God, and who it is that is saying to you, ‘Give me a drink,’ you would have asked him, and he would have given you living water” (John 4:10). By this he means the immortal streams of the font of the Holy Spirit. For that all these things are said of the Spirit of God, the evangelist just mentioned explained in so many words. When the Saviour had said, “If anyone thirsts, let him come to me and drink. Whoever believes in me, as the Scripture has said, out of his belly will flow rivers of living water” (John 7:37-38), he at once added, “Now this he said about the Spirit, whom those who believed in him were to receive” (John 7:39).
That the Saviour was anointed with the Holy Spirit; and if the Spirit were a creature, would not the uncreated one have been anointed with his own handiwork? And that we too have his anointing.

Creation is anointed in baptism with created oil that has been made holy. The Saviour, as God, was anointed with the all-holy Spirit, who is uncreated with him, above us who are his fellows. For if the Spirit were a creature, would not the uncreated one have been anointed with his own handiwork? The witnesses are those set down below. Isaiah, speaking for the Saviour: “The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he has anointed me” (Isaiah 61:1). And David: “Therefore God, your God, has anointed you with the oil of gladness above your fellows” (Psalm 45:7). What is this “therefore”? Because, being God not made with hands, he was anointed by God, uncreated and without beginning. And he said “your God” because of his birth from a virgin.

Peter in the Acts: “You know the word that went out through all Judea and Samaria, beginning from Galilee after the baptism which John preached: Jesus of Nazareth, how God anointed him with the Holy Spirit and with power” (Acts 10:37-38). The Acts again: “They were gathered together in truth in this city against your holy servant Jesus, whom you anointed” (Acts 4:27).

The Song too speaks of this, in these words: “Your name is ointment poured out; therefore the maidens have loved you” (Song of Songs 1:3). It says that Christ bears the name of “ointment,” the name of the Paraclete, since both hypostases share the name, and in themselves give off the fragrance of the nature of God the Father. By “maidens” it means the churches in which he is glorified. Of them David too spoke in the sixty-eighth Psalm: “Rulers went in front, close behind those singing psalms, in the midst of maidens playing timbrels” (Psalm 68:25). He put it so because their faith is proclaimed far and wide, and because they ring out into all the earth with their readings and their singing of psalms.

And in the Song the Bridegroom himself, fair in his beauty, speaks chastely to each of them: “Behold, you are fair, my companion; behold, you are fair” (Song of Songs 1:15; Song of Songs 4:1). And again he sings, as it were, a wedding song: “Come from Lebanon, bride, come from Lebanon; you shall come and pass on from the beginning of faith” (Song of Songs 4:8 LXX).

That we too receive an anointing in our renewal, John writes in his first letter: “And you have an anointing from the Holy One, and you know all things” (1 John 2:20). As the Saviour was anointed in his saving dispensation, he says, so “you too have an anointing from the Holy” Spirit.

And that this saving gift has been furnished to us by the blessed Trinity in common, they teach as follows. Isaiah: “And the Lord of hosts will make for all the nations on this mountain: they shall drink wine, they shall be anointed with ointment on this mountain. Hand on all these things to the nations” (Isaiah 25:6-7 LXX). For by “mountain” he foretold the Church of God, because of the loftiness of the faith; by “wine,” the Lord’s saving blood; by “ointment,” the oil with which, once made holy, we are anointed by the priest. John, in the same first letter, about Christ: “And as for you, the anointing which you received from him abides in you, and you have no need that anyone should teach you; but as his anointing teaches you about all things” (1 John 2:27). And Paul in the second letter to the Corinthians: “Now he who establishes us with you in Christ, and has anointed us, is God, who has also sealed us and given the pledge of the Spirit in our hearts” (2 Corinthians 1:21-22).

choices.issue: Dropped half the section, misattribution, mistranslation
choices.choice: 2026-11-11 (claude-sumfix2-e-u16): retranslated. The old English opened with the stray word 'unmade' and dropped everything from 'inhabited world' through Acts 4:27: Baruch 3:10-13, John 4:10, John 7:37-39, the chapter title 6.23 and its proofs (Isaiah 61:1, Psalm 45:7, Acts 10:37-38, Acts 4:27). It made 'the Paraclete' the speaker of the Song comment, read λιβάνου as 'frankincense', made the Bride 'he', rendered the Isaiah 25 comment 'as was foretold', and printed '7.' before the chapter title. All references added, every one checked against the KJV text or by hand; 'Canticles' replaced; brackets '[epistle]', '[He is]' removed.

choices.why: The section opens mid-sentence (previous section: 'what each city is to men, this, to the Almighty, is the'); only the word this section holds is translated.

choices.english: who did not have the Holy Spirit
choices.why: The genitive plural refers to the Chaldeans, not the exiled people.
Didymus' compound: the Spirit shares the Son's uncreated being.

choices.english: if the Spirit were a creature
choices.why: The subject is unexpressed in the Greek; English needs it, and the argument makes it the Spirit. Not bracketed because it is plain from the sentence.

choices.english: above us who are his fellows
choices.why: Echoes Psalm 45:7 'above your fellows', quoted next.

choices.term: «μύρου» ὄνομα εἶναι τῷ Χριστῷ λέγει τὸ τοῦ παρακλήτου
choices.english: It says that Christ bears the name of “ointment,” the name of the Paraclete
choices.why: The subject is the Song (λέγει), not the Paraclete, as the old English had it; Christ shares the Spirit's name 'ointment', as the next clause says both hypostases share it.
Song of Songs 4:8 LXX has Λιβάνου (Lebanon); the copy-text's lower case λιβάνου does not make it 'frankincense' here.
The Greek Song's rendering of 'the top of Amana'; kept as Didymus read it and marked LXX.
Feminine: addressed to the bride (the Church), not 'he' as in the old English.
Greek Psalm 67 = English 68; verse 26 in Greek = 68:25.

choices.english: As the Saviour was anointed in his saving dispensation
choices.why: Elliptic Greek ('as in the dispensation the Saviour'); 'was anointed' is supplied from the sentence and the chapter title, without brackets.
Governs all three readings (mountain, wine, ointment); the old English attached it only to the last.

choices.term: Περὶ τῶν θεϊκῶν ἐνεργειῶν καὶ παροχῶν
choices.english: On the divine workings and gifts of the Holy Spirit.
choices.why: Chapter title of book 7, set as its own paragraph; the printed '7.' is an edition number and is dropped.

choices.term: κυρίου 67 ἐπ' ἐμέ; ἐκή ρυξεν; τυμπα νιστριῶν; πάν τα
choices.why: 67 is a printed page number, skipped; the other three are words split across printed lines.
The sentence runs into the next unit (its object and verb, 'most caring divine activity ... displays', are there); only the words this section holds are translated, ending with '…'.
